problem_text:
A logistics firm is assembling a shipment of specialized cargo modules to maximize total profit while adhering to a total vehicle weight limit.

The available modules are:
* Module A: weight 29kg, profit 110 units
* Module B: weight 45kg, profit 239 units
* Module C: weight 33kg, profit 13 units
* Module D: weight 17kg, profit 135 units
* Module E: weight 3kg, profit 126 units
* Module F: weight 49kg, profit 171 units
* Module G: weight 47kg, profit 269 units
* Module H: weight 18kg, profit 26 units
* Module I: weight 26kg, profit 197 units
* Module J: weight 45kg, profit 116 units
* Module K: weight 16kg, profit 106 units
* Module L: weight 21kg, profit 19 units
* Module M: weight 40kg, profit 63 units
* Module N: weight 4kg, profit 55 units
* Module O: weight 15kg, profit 191 units
* Module P: weight 39kg, profit 64 units
* Module Q: weight 35kg, profit 210 units
* Module R: weight 18kg, profit 112 units
* Module S: weight 12kg, profit 234 units
* Module T: weight 29kg, profit 244 units
* Module U: weight 15kg, profit 57 units
* Module V: weight 50kg, profit 266 units
* Module W: weight 36kg, profit 103 units
* Module X: weight 45kg, profit 73 units
* Module Y: weight 22kg, profit 104 units
* Module Z: weight 5kg, profit 142 units
* Module AA: weight 46kg, profit 231 units

Furthermore, due to compatibility requirements, exactly one of Module A or Module B must be included in the shipment.

If Module C is selected, it necessitates special handling equipment that reduces the effective vehicle capacity by 10 kg.
The vehicle can transport a maximum of 532 kg. The firm must determine which modules to load.
